title: Perfect cores under finite field extensions
statement: Let $p$ be prime and let $K\subseteq L$ be fields of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-field]. Assume $L$ is finite-dimensional as a vector space over $K$, meaning that finitely many elements of $L$ span $L$ over $K$. For $E=K,L$, define $E_{\mathrm{perf}}=\bigcap_{n\geq0}\{y^{p^n}:y\in E\}$, a subfield of $E$. Then every $x\in L_{\mathrm{perf}}$ is algebraic over $K_{\mathrm{perf}}$: there is a nonzero polynomial $P(T)\in K_{\mathrm{perf}}[T]$ with $P(x)=0$ in $L$. No separability hypothesis on $L/K$ is imposed.

source.place: Expose IV, Lemma 3.2.2 and Proposition 3.2.3(ii), p. 56: finite-extension perfect-core consequence, including the bounded purely inseparable part.

proof.text: Because L is finite-dimensional over K, each element of L is algebraic over K: the powers of an element are linearly dependent over K, yielding a nonzero polynomial relation. Let S be the relative separable closure of K in L, namely the subfield of elements separable algebraic over K. The existing separable-core theorem gives that L/S is purely inseparable (and S/K is separable algebraic).

source.place: Expose IV, Proposition 3.2.3(ii), p. 56, with the relative separable core described before the proposition

proof.text: The finite K-spanning set of L also spans L over S, because K is contained in S. Thus L/S is finite-dimensional. Apply the bounded-exponent Mathlib leaf to this purely inseparable extension, obtaining e such that y^(p^e) lies in S for every y in L. Fix x in L_perf. For each n choose y_n in L with y_n^(p^(n+e))=x. Put z_n=y_n^(p^e). Then z_n lies in S and z_n^(p^n)=y_n^(p^(e+n))=x. Taking n=0 shows x lies in S, and all n show x lies in S_perf. By the existing embedding theorem, the separable algebraic extension S/K admits a K-embedding sigma into the fixed separable closure K^sep (which is separably closed). For every n, sigma(z_n)^(p^n)=sigma(z_n^(p^n))=sigma(x), so sigma(x) lies in every p^n-power image in K^sep.

source.place: Expose IV, Proposition 3.2.3(ii), p. 56, reduction through the bounded purely inseparable tail

proof.text: Apply the perfect-core equality of ILO Lemma 3.2.2 to K and K^sep. It says that sigma(x) is separable algebraic over K_perf, so choose a nonzero polynomial P(T)=sum_i a_i T^i over K_perf with P(sigma(x))=0. Since sigma is a K-algebra map, it fixes every a_i in K_perf, and sigma(sum_i a_i x^i)=sum_i a_i sigma(x)^i=0. Injectivity of sigma gives P(x)=0 in S and hence in L. The polynomial is still nonzero since the coefficient inclusions are injective. This proves the stated algebraicity.

source.place: Expose IV, Lemma 3.2.2 and Proposition 3.2.3(ii), p. 56
